title: William Daley and Paul Ryan Named Chair and Vice Chair of the CSIS Board of Trustees
gist: Press release: CSIS named former Obama chief of staff/Clinton commerce secretary William Daley chair and former House Speaker Paul Ryan vice chair of its board of trustees, succeeding Tom Pritzker (chair since 2015) — a deliberately bipartisan leadership pairing at a major Washington national-security think tank.

insights.claim: CSIS appointed William Daley, former White House chief of staff (2011-2012) and U.S. commerce secretary (1997-2000), as chair of its board of trustees, succeeding Tom Pritzker, who chaired the board since 2015.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Leadership change at an influential DC policy shop; signals continuity rather than a strategic pivot.

insights.claim: Former House Speaker Paul Ryan, who previously chaired the House Ways and Means and Budget Committees, was appointed vice chair of the CSIS board, creating a Democrat-Republican leadership pairing.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Pairing signals CSIS positioning itself as a bipartisan convener on national and economic security debates.
insights.locator: Daley served as White House chief

insights.claim: CSIS frames its institutional value as being at the center of national security and economic security policy debates, explicitly linking the two domains.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Economic security (trade, tech controls) increasingly treated as national security in DC policy circles.
insights.quote: CSIS is at the center of the most important national security and economic security policy debates facing our country

insights.claim: Outgoing chair Tom Pritzker described his tenure as a period of extraordinary institutional change and growth at CSIS, and the new leaders were elected unanimously by the board.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Low signal for markets; confirms institutional stability.
insights.quote: a period of extraordinary institutional change and growth
